instructions: Fill a large pot with water, add 1 tbsp of the salt, and bring it to a boil over high heat.
Slice the mushrooms about 1/4 inch thick. Thinly slice the onion. Mince the garlic.

Heat the olive oil and 1 tbsp of the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add half the mushrooms in a single layer with 1/4 tsp of the salt. Leave them alone for 3 minutes, then stir and cook for 3 more minutes, until deep brown. Transfer them to a bowl and repeat with the rest.
Cook the noodles in the boiling water as the package says. Drain and set aside.
Return all the mushrooms to the skillet. Add the remaining 2 tbsp butter and the onion. Cook for 5 minutes, until the onion is soft.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute.
Stir in the broth, Dijon, soy sauce and thyme. Simmer over medium heat for 3 minutes, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Take the skillet off the heat and let it sit for a minute. Stir in the sour cream and the black pepper. Boiling it will make the sour cream split.
Chop 2 tbsp of the parsley and stir it in. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve over the egg noodles, with the rest of the parsley on top.
method_notes: Salt and Lavender (the lead, 4.75 from 8 votes, no version had 20 ratings) cooks the onion and mushrooms in butter and oil, thickens with a little flour and vegetable broth, and stirs in sour cream off the heat. Dinners, Dishes and Desserts and Berly's Kitchen agree on the method and add thyme and wine. I replaced the Worcestershire sauce, which contains anchovy, with soy sauce and kept Dijon. I browned the mushrooms in two batches for more flavor, and used one pound for four.
